title: EBS Volume Expanded but Linux Filesystem Not Resized
symptom: AWS console shows EBS volume size increased from 20GB to 50GB, but `df -h` still displays 20GB available.
initial_observations: lsblk shows disk is 50G, but partition or filesystem is 20G.
environment: EC2 instance with modified EBS volume (ext4 or xfs).

possible_causes.cause: Partition and filesystem have not been grown to fill the new block device boundary
possible_causes.evidence_needed: lsblk shows xvda is 50G but xvda1 is 20G.
possible_causes.remediation: Run `sudo growpart /dev/xvda 1` to expand partition, followed by `sudo resize2fs /dev/xvda1` (ext4) or `sudo xfs_growfs -d /` (XFS).

investigation_steps.title: Compare Block Devices vs Filesystems
investigation_steps.explanation: Inspect hardware block size vs partition table vs mounted filesystem.
investigation_steps.what_to_look_for: Discrepancy between root disk size and partition size.

prevention: Include filesystem resize commands in provisioning automation after EBS volume modification.
